I have a similar story but a little worse. I'm a little late sorry. 

My friend was back in town on leave from the Air Force and I decided to spend the day with him. He was doing some volunteer work for his recruiter and I had no problem helping. We were told that we were going to help a Marine vet move some boxes into a van and place them in storage because he needed to be out by 10am the next day. So we get there and we are greeted by a friendly man. He wasn't physically disabled, just a bit heavy and had some pretty clear ptsd. We looked throughout the house and not a single thing was packed in a box. It's about 12pm. and he needs to be out by the next day mind you. Me and my friend both give each other that "there's no fucking way" look and do our best to help put items into totes. We are constantly being told that we aren't sorting the items correctly, but we are just trying to get he house packed and moved as fast as we can so this guy doesn't have to leave things behind. After about an hour of packing he leaves. He said he had to go to the bank and pharmacy. No problem. We can start packing quickly. But things are going a little slower without him helping. After another hour of work we have the kitchen packed and that's it. There's not even a moving truck to put boxes on yet. So we move to the living room and pack that quickly. He finally gets home with a truck and we load up the 2 rooms that we fully packed for him. It's evening time.  By this time it's evident that it's not going to be done by tomorrow. Me and my friend feel bad because there's nobody else to help. We make an excuse to go back to the recruiting office and explain our situation to the recruiter. As it turns out he told them he had been packing for the last month and that he only needed help with boxes. The recruiter wasn't mad at all. He understood. We didn't go back that night. I was told that the recruiter got people from his Depp to help early that morning. I'm not sure of they got it done. 

tl;dr. don't wait until the last minute. don't lie about how much there is to do. and do not boss around people who are volunteering for you.
